scope: Public-source metadata and security inventory for RubyGems.org and RubyGems package specifications.
coverage: Public documentation, API schemas, service-status metadata, and publicly disclosed security information. This is not a scan of private RubyGems infrastructure, user accounts, private API keys, or nonpublic telemetry.

metadata_layers.gem_metadata_constraints: RubyGems specification metadata is a string-to-string hash; keys may be up to 128 bytes and values up to 1024 bytes, with UTF-8/no binary data requirements.

current_security_record.topic: Possible leak of legacy API keys via improper cache configuration
current_security_record.status: RubyGems reported that a CDN caching bug could expose one account's legacy API key to another user for up to an hour under affected authentication conditions.
current_security_record.scope: RubyGems stated that legacy keys were revoked; scoped keys created through the UI/CLI and short-lived OIDC/trusted-publisher keys were not affected by this specific issue.
current_security_record.remediation: RubyGems reported deploying cache-control and Vary-header changes in commit d3d11c0 on 2026-07-09, purging affected cached objects, and revoking legacy keys.
current_security_record.abuse_assessment: RubyGems reported no evidence of malicious use in the access-log window it reviewed, while noting that the available logs covered only a recent portion of the estimated exposure period.

security_controls_publicly_documented.description: RubyGems describes push-time checks over gem contents, metadata, and checksums.
RubyGems has publicly described automated static and dynamic analysis, behavioral checks, metadata review, risk scoring, and manual escalation for higher-risk gems.
RubyGems documents short-lived OIDC/trusted-publisher credentials as distinct from legacy API keys.
RubyGems.org publishes component status, incidents, maintenance, and uptime information through its status service.

research_boundaries: Use public APIs and documentation only
Do not collect or publish API keys, passwords, tokens, or private account data
Do not probe private infrastructure or attempt unauthorized access
Do not execute potentially malicious gems as part of metadata collection
Treat a package's metadata or automated risk score as an indicator, not proof of malicious intent
Preserve package version and timestamp because gem metadata changes over time
status: Public RubyGems metadata/security inventory uploaded for repository research.
